A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same query-circuit research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original circuit-discovery experiments, paraphrase ablations, runtime measurements and supplementary analyses in Section 6 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds larger-model evaluations, circuit-overlap analyses and quantitative gender-feature interventions in Section 6 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The BoN, iBoN and BoN-CSM discovery procedures remain unchanged. V2 adds an optional post-discovery SAE procedure for extracting described features from circuit activations and performing feature interventions (Section 6.5; Appendix C.12), extending the interpretation workflow.

E1.justification: Existing dataset coverage is retained. Gender Bias already appeared in v1 Appendix B.5, but v2 adds feature-level bias steering and semantic interpretation as distinct evaluation tasks on it, beyond the earlier circuit-construction comparison.

E2.justification: The original circuit-discovery baselines remain. The new steering experiment adds lowest-NDF circuit selection among ten candidates as a comparator for highest-NDF selection (Table 2). Circuit Tracing receives discussion but is not experimentally benchmarked.

E3.justification: V2 adds fidelity experiments using GPT-2 XL and Llama-3-8B-Instruct, overlap metrics and feature-ablation protocols. Steering evaluation selects 50 of 986 high-bias queries, uses 32 queries for paired comparisons, and separately compares 27 high-NDF against 23 low-NDF queries. Existing benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: New overlap, Jaccard and UpSet analyses investigate shared circuit mechanisms (Section 6.4; Appendix C.11). Gender-feature ablations and an SAE interpretation case study examine actionability and semantic content (Section 6.5; Appendices C.12–C.13). Earlier ablations and complement-circuit analyses remain.

E5.justification: Tables 2 and A7 newly report across-query means and standard deviations, paired Wilcoxon and unpaired Mann–Whitney tests, and Rosenthal's r and Cohen's d. Appendix C.11 specifies sampling seed 2025. These additions do not establish repeated-seed evaluation of the retained benchmarks.

E6.justification: Earlier result plots and runtime values are retained, while scaling, overlap and intervention results are added. Table 2 reports mean logit-bias reductions of 0.810 versus 0.234 for best versus worst circuits. One inconsistency remains: Appendix C.5 claims approximately 0.4 NDF at 5,000 edges, whereas Figure A14(c) shows approximately 0.28 there.

T1.justification: The circuit definitions, attribution equations, NDF definition and NDF–CMD relationship are retained; the latter moves from Appendix C to D. No new proof or substantive derivation is introduced. The new bias-threshold inequality specifies experimental selection.

C1.justification: The central query-circuit, NDF, BoN and sparse-recovery claims remain. The explanatory scope expands modestly through optional SAE-assisted interpretation in v2's introduction, whereas v1 explicitly placed node and edge interpretation outside scope in Section 3.1.

C2.justification: V2 introduces shared-mechanism and actionability interpretations, and expands the necessity/sufficiency interpretation of existing complement-circuit results. New limitations discuss incomplete or polysemantic SAE explanations, unavailable head-specific SAEs, and the remaining need for manual inspection and graph condensation.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-page link and identifies the GPT-2 SAE suite, activation-recording procedure and top-five feature extraction used in the interpretation study. Earlier detailed benchmark settings and runtime disclosures remain. The PDFs alone do not establish the linked resources' availability.

R1.justification: V2 develops the comparison with previously cited Circuit Tracing, explicitly acknowledging its instance-level explanations and describing complementarity with in-place circuits. It adds Gao et al. for the SAE suite and removes the Foote, Shaham and Bricken automated-interpretability references.

P1.justification: Most core exposition and section order are retained. V2 revises the introduction and limitations, relocates pseudocode and runtime discussion into appendices, removes the supplementary contents page, adds an Impact Statement, and updates affiliation and correspondence information.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column presentation, with extensive resizing and repositioning of displays. V2 adds steering tables, overlap plots and circuit visualizations, revises Figure 1's illustration, and relocates existing algorithms and the runtime table.

improvement.justification: V1 principally demonstrated output recovery and left semantic interpretation outside scope. V2 substantially strengthens the evidence for useful explanations through paired feature interventions linking NDF to actionability, circuit-overlap analyses and larger-model evaluations. Selected samples, acknowledged SAE limitations and the Appendix C.5/Figure A14 numerical inconsistency constrain the conclusions, but the added validation addresses an important weakness in the earlier paper.
